items.q: How long does a website take?
items.a: A marketing site typically goes from kickoff to live in 2 to 3 weeks. Larger sites with custom integrations or multilingual content can take 4 to 6 weeks. Either way, you get a fixed launch date in writing before the project starts.

items.q: Do you work with Polish companies? Do you speak Polish?
items.a: Yes. I'm based in Warsaw and work with Polish clients regularly. I speak conversational Polish, fluent English and native Russian / Ukrainian. Contracts can be signed under Polish law and invoicing is handled with VAT EU.

items.q: Can you build a site in Ukrainian for the diaspora market?
items.a: Yes. Several of my projects ship in PL / EN / UA / RU simultaneously. I handle proper i18n routing, hreflang, locale-specific SEO and content translation review with native speakers.

items.q: What happens after the project is delivered?
items.a: You get 30 days of bug-fix support included. After that, edits are billed at €50 per hour with a one-hour minimum. There is no forced monthly retainer — you only pay when you actually need work done.

items.q: How much does an AI chatbot or agent cost?
items.a: AI agents start at €1,200 for a focused use case (a FAQ assistant, a lead qualifier, a single-tool automation). Multi-tool agents with CRM and database integrations typically land between €2,000 and €5,000. Final price after a 30-minute scoping call.

items.q: Do you build for Android as well as iOS?
items.a: Yes — I build cross-platform from a single codebase using React Native and Expo, then submit to both the App Store and Google Play. If a project genuinely needs platform-native, I'll tell you upfront and quote accordingly.

items.q: How is working with you different from hiring an agency?
items.a: You message me directly. No account managers, no junior developers handling your project while a senior signs off. The person you brief is the person writing the code. Decisions take minutes, not weeks.

items.q: Can you build a website that actually ranks on Google?
items.a: Yes — that's the default, not an upsell. Every site I build ships with technical SEO, schema markup, hreflang for multilingual pages, optimized Core Web Vitals and IndexNow pings on deploy. Most pages index within hours and start ranking within weeks.

items.q: Do you sign contracts?
items.a: Always. Every project starts with a written agreement covering scope, payment schedule, IP transfer, deadlines and what happens if either side wants out. Contracts can be in English or Polish.

items.q: What if I need changes after launch?
items.a: Edits are billed at €50 per hour, with a one-hour minimum. No forced monthly retainer. You can come back six months later for a small change and I'll handle it — same terms, same rate.

items.q: How fast can you ship?
items.a: A marketing site lands in 2–3 weeks from kickoff. A larger project with integrations and multilingual content takes 4–6 weeks. The date is in writing before the project starts.

items.q: Will it actually be faster than my current site?
items.a: Almost always, yes. A typical WordPress on shared hosting yields LCP of 3–5 seconds. My sites consistently sit under 1 second. It's not 'optimization' — it's a different architecture (static + edge).

items.q: Who maintains the content?
items.a: Depends on the CMS we pick. Sanity for teams who want Notion-style editing. MDX for teams that update once a month. We decide on the discovery call.

items.q: Can you connect my analytics and pixels?
items.a: Yes. GA4, Meta Pixel, Yandex Metrika, Plausible, PostHog — plus server-side conversion tracking if it matters.

items.q: What if I already have a Figma design?
items.a: Great. I'll build from it — and I'll usually flag anything that needs tightening for production (accessibility, states, mobile breakpoints) before we start.

items.q: Does a multilingual site cost extra?
items.a: Less than you'd expect, because i18n is part of my stack, not a bolt-on plugin. The first language sets the structure; each extra locale mainly adds content and translation review, not a second build. A four-language site (EN/PL/UA/RU) usually lands a few hundred euros above a single-language one — exact figure after the discovery call.

items.q: Who owns the code, domain and hosting once it's done?
items.a: You do, all of it. The domain and hosting (Vercel) are registered in your name, the source code lives in your GitHub, and the IP transfer is written into the contract. Nothing is rented or locked to me — bring in another developer later and they inherit a clean repo and carry on.

items.title: Sales bots

items.body: Not a black box. Dashboard with dialogs, tags, response rating, exports and manual overrides.

items.title: Model-agnostic
items.body: GPT-5 / Claude / Gemini — we pick per task and budget. Swap without rewriting the project.

items.q: Is this a GPT wrapper or something real?
items.a: Real. Function calling, tools, RAG, dialog classification, backend logic, integrations — what separates a working agent from a chat wrapper.

items.q: What does it cost to run?
items.a: Depends on volume. A typical sales agent on GPT-4o-mini / Gemini Flash sits around €30–80/month in API at 1000+ dialogs. Full estimate on the discovery call.

items.q: Will it hallucinate?
items.a: Almost never in a well-built RAG. I enforce a strict-citation mode: if the answer isn't in the corpus, the agent says 'I don't know' and routes to a human. Controllable.

items.q: How does it connect to my CRM?
items.a: Through the native API. AmoCRM v4, HubSpot, Pipedrive — webhooks and REST. The bot tags, moves through the pipeline, leaves notes. Everything a manager does manually — automatic.

items.q: What if a 2x better model comes out tomorrow?
items.a: Plug it in. The architecture is provider-agnostic through an abstraction layer. Swapping GPT for Claude or Gemini is a day's work, not a week.

items.q: How long does it take to launch an AI agent?
items.a: A focused bot — a FAQ assistant or a lead qualifier — ships in 1–2 weeks from kickoff. An agent with RAG over your knowledge base and a CRM integration takes 3–4 weeks. I fix the scope and date in writing before we start, then show progress as we build.

items.q: Can one bot answer in several languages on my own data?
items.a: Yes. A single agent handles Polish, Russian, Ukrainian and English, replying in whatever language the customer writes in. The RAG layer is built on your documents and knowledge base, so answers come from your sources — not the model's general knowledge. Your data stays yours and is never used to train anyone else's model.

automation.lead: I connect your tools into one flow that runs itself: a lead comes in — data is enriched, lands in your CRM, the team gets pinged, the report builds itself. No copy-paste, no forgotten leads.

items.title: Leads & enquiries
items.body: Leads from your site, forms, ads and messengers land in your CRM with fields filled — no manual re-entry.

items.title: CRM pipeline
items.body: Deals move through stages automatically: tags, tasks for managers, reminders — AmoCRM, HubSpot, Pipedrive.

items.title: Notifications
items.body: Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, email — the team hears about what matters in seconds, not the next day.

items.title: Documents & reports
items.body: Contracts and quotes generated from templates, exports to Google Sheets, daily and weekly reports on autopilot.

items.title: Data sync
items.body: Site, CRM, sheets, inventory, accounting — data moves between systems via API, no duplicates, no drift.

items.title: AI in the loop
items.body: Where decisions are needed: email classification, enquiry parsing, conversation summaries, on-brand replies.

items.q: How is this different from an AI agent?
items.a: An AI agent is a conversation — a bot talks to your customer. Automation is the plumbing between systems: lead → CRM → notification → report, no human in between. They often run together: the agent talks, the automation moves data behind the scenes.

items.q: Do you build on Make, Zapier or code?
items.a: Depends on the job. Simple flows go on Make or n8n — fast and cheap to maintain. Complex logic, load and non-standard APIs I build in Node.js. I often mix: no-code for the skeleton, code for the critical steps.

items.q: What does it cost to run per month?
items.a: On n8n on your own server — near zero, just hosting. On Make/Zapier — their usage-based subscription, usually €20–100/mo. I size it to your volume on the discovery call.

items.q: What if one of the services changes its API?
items.a: I build in error handling and failure alerts — if a step breaks, you know immediately, not a week later through vanished leads. Fixes are covered by support.

items.q: How long does it take to set up?
items.a: A single flow (lead → CRM → notification) takes 3–7 days. A chain of several processes with enrichment and reports is 2–3 weeks. Scope and date fixed in writing before we start.

items.q: Can you connect to my system?
items.a: If it has an API or webhooks — almost certainly yes. AmoCRM, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Telegram, WhatsApp, Google Workspace, Notion, hundreds of apps via Make/Zapier. If the API is closed, I'll tell you straight on the call.

items.q: Isn't native better?
items.a: For 90% of product tasks — no. Expo / React Native gives native perf and full hardware access. Native code makes sense only for AR, heavy graphics or specialized hardware. I'll tell you honestly.

items.q: Who submits to the stores?
items.a: I do. Including review responses. Apple Developer Account and Google Play Console under your legal entity — I work under your accounts.

items.q: How long is an MVP?
items.a: Typically 4–6 weeks from kickoff to TestFlight / Internal Testing. Another 1–2 weeks to the public stores (depends on Apple review).

items.q: What if Apple rejects it?
items.a: Standard, not scary. I've been through review enough times to usually predict what they'll ask. If they reject — we fix and resubmit, no extra charge.

items.q: Can we add web later?
items.a: Yes. Expo Router lets one codebase target iOS + Android + Web. If your product goes that way, the path is short.

items.q: Who owns the code and the app once it's delivered?
items.a: You do — fully. The source code, your App Store Connect and Google Play accounts, the backend and all keys are set up under your legal entity and transferred to you by contract. I don't hold the project hostage or lock you in: you can keep building it yourself or hand it to any other developer.

items.q: What does it cost to run the app after launch?
items.a: Less than agencies make you fear. Backend hosting and services are typically €10–50/month depending on load; the store accounts are $99/year for Apple and a one-time $25 for Google. Updates and fixes for new iOS/Android versions are €50/hour with no forced retainer — you only pay when something actually needs doing.

items.q: How much should I budget for ads?
items.a: For local lead-gen in Poland, €500–1,500/month of ad spend is a realistic start — separate from my management fee. We set the budget to your goal on the first call and scale only once the numbers work.

items.q: What's the difference between setup and management?
items.a: Setup (from €300) is the one-time build: account structure, tracking, conversions and first campaigns. Management (€500/month) is the ongoing work — optimization, A/B tests, reporting and scaling. Many clients start with setup and add management once leads come in.

items.q: When will I see results?
items.a: Search campaigns can bring leads in the first week. Meta and Performance Max need 2–4 weeks to exit the learning phase. Real optimization comes from data, so the first month is about gathering it.

items.q: Do you work with both Google Ads and Meta?
items.a: Yes — and I run them together. The same conversion goals, one dashboard, budget shifted to whichever channel is cheaper per lead this month.

items.q: Who owns the accounts?
items.a: You do. I work inside your Google Ads and Meta Business accounts, or set them up in your name. If we part ways, everything stays with you — data, pixels and history.

items.q: Google Ads or Meta — which is right for my business?
items.a: It depends on demand. If people already search for your service on Google, starting with Search captures the hottest leads and usually a better cost-per-acquisition for B2B and local services. Meta is stronger when demand needs warming up — new audiences, retargeting, a visual product. On the call I look at your niche and often suggest starting with one channel, then adding the second once it pays back.

items.q: How do you charge — a percentage of ad spend?
items.a: No. A flat €500/month to manage, with no cut of your ad spend — so I have zero incentive to inflate the budget whether you spend €500 or €5,000. You pay the ad budget straight to Google and Meta from your own card. Your Looker Studio report shows cost per lead and ROAS, so you see exactly where the money works.

donbrava.title: AI sales manager
donbrava.tagline: Replies to clients from the owner's real Telegram account — mirrors his writing style, his timing and the "typing…" indicator. Clients never realise they're chatting with an AI, not a real person.
donbrava.problem: Bohdan is an immigration consultant in Slovakia, handling temporary protection (€350/person) and business services for Ukrainians (€200 paid consultations, residency, s.r.o., živnosť). Inbound on Telegram was steady, but quality suffered: evening messages sat until morning, weekends ate leads, and recurring 'what documents?' / 'how long does it take?' questions soaked up more time than the actual paying clients.
donbrava.solution: I built a Telegram userbot on Telethon + GPT-4o that runs from Bohdan's real phone number — not a @bot, a live account. It imitates his messaging style and timing (2–12 minute unread windows on first contact, a typing indicator, an explicit read-receipt delay), distinguishes services (€350 temporary protection vs €200 consultation), pulls the live EUR→UAH rate from Monobank's public API, sends the right payment details (IBAN or Mono card with the converted hryvnia amount), flags payments with a [PAYMENT_SENT] marker and quietly hands the conversation over to Bohdan. Document uploads and escalations ping the owner instantly with a deep link into the chat.
results: ≈ 210 hours of owner time returned per month — the equivalent of 1.3 full-time staff
Full 24/7 coverage — no more lost evening or weekend leads
Payment details land before the prospect can DM a competitor
Run cost ≈ €30/month in API — vs ≥ €1,200/month for a junior sales hire
donbrava.quote: The bot writes the way I do — clients have no idea it isn't me. I open Telegram in the morning and three payments are already in, plus three notifications in the owner chat.

bodyforge.title: Body Forge — AI Fitness Coach
bodyforge.tagline: A native iOS app for the gym: AI workout analysis, live set tracking, and programmes that respond to your real numbers.
bodyforge.problem: Lifters who track workouts in a notes app lose the only data that matters — set-by-set context. Notes don't remember last week's weight. Generic 'gym tracker' apps drown the screen in graphs and never tell you what to do next. The brief was a coach in your pocket: clean tracking during the set, real analysis after, and a programme that actually adapts as you progress.
bodyforge.solution: I built a native SwiftUI app for iOS. During a workout it shows the bare minimum: last week's sets, a rest timer, weight, reps — one tap to log a set. After the session, an AI coach on GPT-4o reads the whole workout — volume, intensity, progression vs the last three weeks — and writes a short, personal post-workout analysis with concrete pickups for next time ('stalled on incline press 3 weeks running — deload to 80% next week'). Programmes are first-class: an Upper/Lower split, full-body for beginners, custom blocks. The library has 200+ exercises with video form demos. Localised RU + EN.
results: Live in the App Store — Body Forge: AI Fitness Coach
AI coach delivers a personal post-workout analysis in ~10 seconds
Workout screen optimised for one-handed use between sets
Programme library + activity rings + Apple Health heart-rate integration
bodyforge.quote: The post-workout analysis is the thing. It's like having a coach who actually looks at the numbers and doesn't pretend everything is fine when you stalled.
